data_leaves_device: app install/usage telemetry (phone-side; the BLE device itself has no network interface)

endpoints.name: Firmware info / OTA check
endpoints.returns: Latest .ufw firmware metadata, keyed by product type; the app falls back to the 14 .ufw images bundled in its assets.

endpoints.name: BLE advertised-name filter list (extends the default IDL prefix)

cloud.failure_mode: Nothing user-visible stops working. The device is driven entirely over local BLE with no account and no pairing; the cloud only feeds the app's firmware check, advertised-name filter list and pattern library, and firmware images are bundled inside the app itself.
cloud.notes: Endpoint set read from the vendor app's networking layer. Cloud request signing uses a separate app-side key that is NOT part of the BLE protocol and is not recorded here.

manufacturer_data.description: Manufacturer-data (AD type 0xFF) payload starts with 0x54 0x52 0x00 0x61 ("TR" + 0x0061; company_id 21076 = 0x5254 is the "TR" prefix little-endian). A scan-response filter in the vendor app matches the same prefix followed by 0x14. Adv field layout: byte 6 = device group id, byte 7 = vendor/device id, bytes 11-12 = lamp count (uint16 LE).

Not an assigned identifier: 0x5254 little-endian spells "TR", the first two bytes of the family's 54 52 00 xx advertisement prefix (same squat as shining-glasses.yaml / magic-display.yaml). iDeal LED units use 54 52 00 61 — see discovery for the payload match.

device.name: iDeal LED Pixel Strings & Trees
device.notes:
Addressable RGB pixel strings, curtain lights and pixel trees (firmware product codes TR21xx/TR22xx/TR23xx; ~14 product-keyed firmware images are bundled in the vendor app assets) driven by the iDeal LED app (com.tech.idealled, analyzed v3.0.4). Member of the Heaton OEM app family shared with Magic Display and Shining Glasses: same 16-byte [len][ASCII opcode] command framing, same d44bc439-...-1296xx characteristic set, same AES-128-ECB command encryption — but a JieLi control chip (JieLi OTA service 0xAE00) and a string/tree opcode set. Sibling specs: magic-display.yaml (panel opcodes, Quintic), idotmatrix.yaml (different, CRC32-framed upload protocol — cross-linked as family, not as wire-compatible), shining-glasses.yaml.
COMMAND FRAMING (HIGH — vendor-app static analysis, corroborated by 8none1/idealLED): every command is a 16-byte block — byte 0 = payload length (count of the meaningful bytes that follow), bytes 1..n = ASCII opcode (4-9 chars) plus parameter bytes, remainder zero-padded. The whole block is AES-128-ECB encrypted (single block, no IV) before the write to characteristic ...9600. Notifications on ...9601 are decrypted with the same key and then matched as plaintext ASCII ack strings: MULTOK, MULTCPOK, MULTREOK, SGLSOK, PLACPOK, PLAREOK, LAMPNMAX+value, LAMPNCANNOT, ERROR. Recovered AES keys recorded per clean-room convention: the static key on the characteristics below is the one PUBLISHED by the open-source 8none1/idealLED project (and matches the key independently recovered from the vendor app's bundled native crypto library; it is byte-identical to the Magic Display family key).
DISCOVERY: the vendor app's scanner gates on the 0xFFF0 service UUID — in v3.0.4 the advertised-name filter (default prefix "IDL", cloud-extendable) is stubbed off, so the service UUID is the operative gate. The manufacturer-specific advertisement (AD type 0xFF) starts with 54 52 00 61 ("TR" + 0x0061); a scan-response filter matches that prefix followed by 0x14. Parsed adv fields (vendor app's adv parser): byte 6 = device group id, byte 7 = vendor/device id, bytes 11-12 = lamp count (uint16 LE). CAUTION (8none1): devices advertising as "IDL" or "ISP" lights exist that speak a DIFFERENT protocol — confirm 0xFFF0 plus the d44bc439 characteristics before driving.
POST-CONNECT (MEDIUM — order not pinned by static analysis): the app sends a CONNECT handshake (+7B, payload undecoded), CONFIRM +2B for RGB channel order (parameter bytes are ASCII 'G'=0x47, 'B'=0x42, 'R'=0x52), CHECKLINE +00/01 link check, and LAMPQ lamp-count queries (reply LAMPNMAX+val or LAMPNCANNOT); LEDS+1B / LEDFIRST / LEDSECOND configure LED counts and daisy-chain position. The ...9602 characteristic reads a firmware version (decrypted payload contains 52 00 61 82..., version bytes at [6],[7]).
BULK TRANSFERS: multicolor lists, doodle frames and images are fragmented as [chunk_len+1][frame_index][data...] with 96-byte chunks when an MTU was negotiated, else 18 (MEDIUM — from the app's fragmentation builder; whether bulk fragments on ...960a are additionally ECB-encrypted is UNVERIFIED — sibling Magic Display encrypts 16-byte blocks on its bulk channel, but iDeal LED's 96-byte fragment format suggests raw. Capture one MULT upload to settle it). DOOTCP signals doodle transfer completion.
OPCODES BEYOND THE COMMANDS BELOW (seen in the vendor app, layouts not fully decoded — do NOT guess payloads, 8none1 bricked a light set with out-of-family bytes): SCHD +8B schedule/timer; MIC / MIC+2B music mode; CAMERA +3B camera color-capture; SCREEN0/SCREEN0CP screen push; BEGU+b upload-begin marker; CALL +2B call notification; DEN +1B; LOCATE; FLASHE; LIDON/LIDOFF; LEWPT +1B (roles uncertain).
OTA: standard JieLi RCSP BLE OTA (jl_bt_ota SDK; native auth library in the app): service 0xAE00, write 0xAE01, notify 0xAE02; firmware is the JieLi .ufw container. Firmware selection keys off productType / vendorId / pid parsed from the TR advertisement. After OTA the device may reconnect with its address minus 1 LSB (the vendor app carries a workaround).
CONFIDENCE: GATT layout, framing, encryption, core opcodes (TURN, LIGHT, COLO, MODE, SPEED, SGLS, CONFIRM, LAMPQ) HIGH — static analysis of the vendor app plus the working open-source implementations (8none1/idealLED with btsnoop captures, koying/ha_ideal_led_ble). MULT header layout, DOOD layout, fragmentation and OTA details MEDIUM (single source: the app). Connect handshake order, SCHD/MIC/CAMERA payloads LOW — live capture needed. Everything app-derived; not yet run against hardware by this repo.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands; the static AES key obfuscates but does not authenticate. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect, enable notifications on ...9601, optionally negotiate MTU (96-byte bulk chunks vs 18), then CONFIRM RGB order and query LAMPQ.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Commands are AES-encrypted with a fixed, publicly documented key, so any client that implements the framing can connect straight away. Identify by the 0xFFF0 service plus the 54 52 00 61 manufacturer-data prefix rather than by name alone — 8none1 reports "IDL"/"ISP"-named lights that speak a different protocol.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link. After a firmware OTA the device may reappear with its address minus 1 LSB (vendor-app workaround observed); rescan rather than assuming the old address.

covers: power, brightness, solid color (G,R,B order), mode, speed
multicolor segment effects (MULT + fragmented RGB upload)
firmware OTA (JieLi .ufw) from app-bundled or cloud-fetched images
not_covered: schedule/timer (SCHD), music mode (MIC), camera capture (CAMERA) — payload layouts undecoded
local_access.summary: Full local control over BLE as shipped: connect to the 0xFFF0 service, AES-128-ECB with the static key recorded on the command characteristic (public via 8none1/idealLED), no pairing, no account, no cloud dependency at any step.

begin_upload.description: Begin-upload marker preceding ANIM/IMAG payload pushes (BEGU + 1 byte). MEDIUM — role inferred.

confirm_rgb_order.description: Confirm RGB channel order (CONFIRM + 2 bytes). Parameter bytes are ASCII channel letters: 'G' = 0x47, 'B' = 0x42, 'R' = 0x52.

doodle_pixel.description: Doodle/freehand draw (DOOD + 7 bytes): two pixel-index bytes (order unverified), mode, speed, then R, G, B. Device signals doodle transfer completion with DOOTCP. A railings/icebar product variant uses an extended 18-byte form [0x12]['DOOD'][0][0][2][100][i][i2][i3]... . Confidence: MEDIUM — layout from the app's draw sender, not captured.

multicolor_effect.description: Multicolor segment effect header (MULT + 6 bytes). Fields per the vendor app's multicolor builder: model_index = effect model index minus 10; direction = !reverse (1 = normal); the 100 is a literal; then speed, color_count, saturation. After this header, the RGB triplets are sent fragmented on the bulk channel (...960a): fragments [chunk_len+1][frame_index][data...], 96-byte chunks with a negotiated MTU else 18. Device acks on notify: MULTCPOK (header accepted), MULTOK (complete), MULTREOK (re-send fragment). Confidence: MEDIUM — single source, verify with a capture.

placement_complete.description: Placement transfer complete (PLACP). Device acks PLACPOK (accepted) or PLAREOK (re-send).

power_on.description: Power on (TURN 0x01). Plaintext shown; encrypt before write.

query_lamp_count.description: Query lamp-strip count (LAMPQ). Reply on notify: LAMPNMAX+value, or LAMPNCANNOT if unsupported.

select_effect.description: Select built-in effect (SGLS + 1 byte index). Device acks SGLSOK on the notify channel.

set_color.description: Set solid color (COLO + 3 bytes). NOTE the parameter order is G, R, B — not R, G, B.

set_led_count.description: LED-count config (LEDS + 1 byte); part of the LEDFIRST/LEDSECOND config sequence.

characteristics.name: Command (WRITE1)
characteristics.notes: Main command channel. Plaintext is a 16-byte block [payload_len][ASCII opcode][params][zero pad]; the block is AES-128-ECB encrypted before the write. The static key is the one PUBLISHED by the open-source 8none1/idealLED project (see helpful_urls); it matches the key independently recovered from the vendor app's bundled native crypto library and is byte-identical to the Magic Display family key. Recorded per the repo's recovered-key convention. Confidence: HIGH. Do NOT send out-of-family bytes — the 8none1 author bricked a light set that way (see helpful_urls).

characteristics.name: Notification
characteristics.notes: Device replies arrive here encrypted with the same AES-128-ECB key (decrypt, then match plaintext ASCII from byte 1): MULTOK, MULTCPOK, MULTREOK, SGLSOK, PLACPOK, PLAREOK, LAMPNMAX+value, LAMPNCANNOT, ERROR. Whether replies longer than 16 bytes are multi-block ECB is unverified.

characteristics.name: Firmware Version
characteristics.notes: Read characteristic for the firmware version. The payload decrypts with the same family key; the decrypted bytes contain 52 00 61 82... with the version at offsets [6] and [7]. Confidence: MEDIUM — layout observed in the vendor app's version parser.

characteristics.name: Bulk Data (WRITE2)
characteristics.notes: Bulk channel for multicolor RGB-triplet lists, doodle frames and image data. Fragment format [chunk_len+1][frame_index][data...], 96-byte chunks when an MTU is negotiated, else 18. Encryption status UNVERIFIED (MEDIUM): sibling Magic Display ECB-encrypts 16-byte blocks on its bulk channel, but this fragment format is not 16-byte aligned, which suggests raw writes — settle with a capture of one MULT upload.

characteristics.name: Auxiliary (WRITE3)
characteristics.notes: Third write characteristic bound by the vendor app's BLE layer; specific role not pinned down (live DIY / realtime data candidate, by family analogy with magic-display.yaml). Confidence: LOW.

characteristics.name: OTA Write
characteristics.notes: Standard JieLi BLE OTA write channel (RCSP/jl_bt_ota SDK); .ufw container format. After OTA the device may reconnect with its BLE address minus 1 LSB — rescan rather than reusing the old address.
